_meta.purpose: The product-intent confirmation register required by the brief: for each submitted link we store the intended ASIN, the official listing URL, the confirmation date and the source, in these fields and only these. The observed redirect target is stored in a separate field and is never merged into the intended value.
_meta.blank_policy: A null means 'not confirmed from an official source'. It is rendered as an empty cell plus a flag, never as an inferred value.

products.candidate_listing_url_basis: mechanical transform: the identifier string from the submitted URL placed into Amazon's /dp/<identifier> pattern. It is a candidate to click, not a confirmed destination.
products.observed_redirect_note: Not observed. This environment has no network route to link.amazon or amazon.com (egress is allowlisted to github/npm/PyPI and one attempt at the /dp/ URL returned a fetch error), so the redirect chain must be recorded by a human inside the enrolled account.
products.assumed_shelf_section_basis: Assigned from the brief's own editorial hypotheses, which are all air-fryer and multi-function-kitchen-appliance topics. No product data supports it. Flagged FLG-005.
products.why_no_fields: Product name, price, availability, rating and commission are blank because none of them can be read from an official source from this session, and every one of them is licence-restricted anyway: prices and ratings may only be shown from Amazon-served links or API data [S06] [S07]. Filling them from a memory of the ASIN, a search snippet, or a third-party listing site would be exactly the 'inaccurate, overbroad or misleading claim' the Participation Requirements prohibit [S16].
products.notes: Identifier as supplied is 9 characters. Amazon's own policies text defines an ASIN only by name, not by length, so this project records the count and the mismatch against widely documented 10-character examples, and stops there. Whether the short link resolves to a valid product page is FLG-003.

buyer_checks.check: The listing page title, brand and model match the exact identifier we linked to, and the seller/fulfilment line is legible.
buyer_checks.why_it_matters: A link that lands on a search-results page or a different variation is not a link to a Product, which the Participation Requirements specifically distinguish [S15].

buyer_checks.check: The address bar after the click still carries tag=shopnow047c-20.
buyer_checks.where: browser address bar immediately after the click
buyer_checks.why_it_matters: The tag has to survive the redirect or the referral is not attributable and the purchase is disqualified [S03] [S04].

buyer_checks.check: The current price, shipping and return terms on the listing, not the price anyone showed you elsewhere.
buyer_checks.why_it_matters: Prices and availability change; third-party cached numbers go stale, and Amazon's own licence caps how long any of it may be stored [S06] [S08].

buyer_checks.check: Whether the model is subject to a recall or safety notice for your market.
buyer_checks.where: the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission recall search
buyer_checks.why_it_matters: Heating appliances are a category where a recall check costs a minute and matters more than any review score. Independent government source; we link out to it rather than reproducing it.

buyer_checks.check: Counter clearance, door swing and cord length in your own kitchen, measured before ordering.
buyer_checks.where: your kitchen, with a tape measure
buyer_checks.why_it_matters: The single most common reason a large small-appliance comes back is that it does not fit where it has to live. Nothing on a listing page can settle that for you.
